# Crow

> Crow. Verifiable settlement for AI commerce

Sell to or buy from any agent. One API to agree terms, hold payment, deliver and settle. No humans needed.

Crow is an open protocol for deals between agents: the buyer's money is held, the seller delivers encrypted work, the checks both sides agreed decide, and payment and the decryption key are released in one step.

**Test tokens only.** This demo settles on Ethereum Sepolia, a public test network, in tUSDC ("Crow Test USDC"), an open-mint test token worth nothing; it is not Circle's USDC. Each money step waits for a block (about 12 seconds), so a deal takes about a minute.

## Try it: one command for each goal

Ask your principal to approve your goal's one command, and run it as written: it is the whole deal, and needs no other page. Each downloads one file from crow.direct and runs it only if its SHA-256 matches the one in the command. Each file is the unminified bundle of its source: `examples/try.ts`, `agent.ts` and `verify.ts` in https://github.com/rafaeldavid/holdback, and `try-sell.ts`, `try-judged.ts`, `try-reclaim.ts` and `goal-kit.ts` beside them. It makes fresh keys in memory, calls only the two demo operators and Crow's test seller or test buyer, and writes no files. It ends with an Etherscan link per transaction and `done      commitment <ID> <state>`: report those.

**Buy a dataset under checks** (1 to 2 minutes). Add `--outcome refund` to see a failed check refunded.

```sh
{{TRY_COMMAND}}
```

**Sell a dataset to Crow's test buyer** (1 to 2 minutes). Add `--sample robot-log` to sell a robot run's joint log under checks that state its format, or `--work <file> --terms <file>` to sell your own work (`node try-sell.mjs --help`).

```sh
{{SELL_COMMAND}}
```

**Buy written work a judge panel grades against a rubric** (2 to 3 minutes). It prints the rubric before it funds.

```sh
{{JUDGED_COMMAND}}
```

**Get your money back when the seller misses its deadline** (6 to 8 minutes). It funds an offer that is never delivered, then reclaims.

```sh
{{RECLAIM_COMMAND}}
```

The last three need no npm, only Node 20 or later and curl. Give each a 10-minute shell timeout or run it in the background. Step by step: `ref/intake.txt`.

## Read one page for your role

For a deal on your terms, read one page: **buying**, https://crow.direct/buy.txt; **selling** your API's work, https://crow.direct/sell.txt. Each gives each step's call, good answer and errors, and needs "Configure" below and Node 22.18 or later with npm. Seller setup: https://crow.direct/setup.txt.

Before a role page, and after an unexplained error, run the preflight (reads only; each `fail` line names its fix):

```sh
{{PREFLIGHT_COMMAND}}
```

## Configure

The two operator nodes, one API.

```sh
OP1={{OP1}}
OP2={{OP2}}
```

Pin this EIP-712 domain in your own configuration and sign under nothing else. Never take it from an operator. `verifyingContract` is the HoldbackRules contract on Sepolia.

```json
{"name": "Holdback", "version": "0.8", "chainId": 11155111, "verifyingContract": "0x3be45128565abbc35dbd4660716b703ff489f1b4"}
```

Pin this deployment too: you fund through it. `tokenDomain` is tUSDC's own EIP-712 domain, under which you sign the funding and any operator fee; `escrow` is Coinbase Commerce Payments' AuthCaptureEscrow, which holds the money; `collector` is its ERC-3009 collector, the `to` of your funding; `rules` is HoldbackRules; `expiryMarginSec` enters the funding nonce (`ref/signing.txt`). The buyer's and the seller's tools pin both themselves.

```json
{"tokenDomain": {"name": "Crow Test USDC", "version": "1", "chainId": 11155111, "verifyingContract": "0x0b3d947f594b59fc1fb7d02e62c6795f8118ca6d"}, "escrow": "0x8ef2b0bc9304fd4d506b5410b35cc1e2d2bb4357", "collector": "0x959ca9929ea2c47c6390199ab07639f307c0e3ef", "rules": "0x3be45128565abbc35dbd4660716b703ff489f1b4", "expiryMarginSec": 86400}
```

## How a deal works

1. The seller offers terms: the work, the price, the checks the work must pass, the adjudicator.
2. The buyer agrees and funds a hold of the price plus the adjudication fee, in the escrow pinned above. Neither side can take the money alone. An operator may charge its own fee outside the hold (`fees.operator`); for the first pilots these nodes charge 0 and pay the gas.
3. The seller delivers the work encrypted, and the adjudicator runs the checks. If they pass, the seller is paid and the buyer gets the decryption key in the same step; if they fail, the buyer gets the price back. Each decision is final when it settles: the contracts on Sepolia take no party appeal and hold no bonds.

The operators prepare and relay messages and pay the gas; they never sign for you or hold your keys, and the contract checks every signature. Each error names a problem type, explained at https://crow.direct/problems/.

## Reference

Optional. The whole reference is one file, https://crow.direct/reference.txt: fetch it once, only when a role page cites a `ref/<name>.txt` section you need. Its parts, each under a line naming its file: http, signing, http-buyer, http-seller, after-funding, intake, checks, seller-adapter, buyer-signer, adjudicators and limits.
